title: Fading Happiness
content:
For a few moments, silence lingered between them.

Sneha quietly looked at Siddu, a gentle smile forming on her lips.

"So..." she asked softly, "you were happy... right?"

A faint smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"Yes," he replied.

"I was."

His smile lingered only for a moment before it slowly faded.

"But..."

"The story didn't end there."

Sneha's expression changed instantly.

The excitement she had felt after hearing Shreya's confession slowly gave way to curiosity.

"Then..." she said, leaning forward slightly, "continue."

Siddu looked at the endless mountains before him. Taking a slow, deep breath, he allowed himself to return to those memories once again.

________________________________________

"After that day..."

"My life completely changed."

"Shreya and I finally became one."

"We started talking every single day."

"Every day, at the same time, without fail."

"No matter how busy we were..."

"We always made time for each other."

"I shared every little moment of my life with her."

"My happiness..."

"My worries..."

"My dreams..."

"Everything."

A gentle smile spread across Siddu's face.

"Those were some of the happiest days of my life."

He chuckled softly.

"At the same time..."

"I was constantly teased by Yashwanth."

"He never missed an opportunity to make fun of me."

Sneha smiled, imagining Siddu being teased by his best friend.

"Then our first semester holidays began."

"I went back home."

"For the first time..."

"I told my father everything."

"About Shreya."

"About how we had met."

"About everything we had gone through."

Siddu's eyes softened.

"Instead of getting angry..."

"He smiled."

"He was genuinely happy for me."

"Then one day he surprised me."

"He asked me to invite Shreya home for lunch."

I looked at Sneha and smiled.

"I never expected my father to say something like that."

"So I called Shreya."

"At first, she was terrified."

"She kept saying..."

"'What if your parents don't like me?'"

"'What if something goes wrong?'"

"I somehow convinced her."

"To come, she told her parents that she was going to one of her friend's houses."

"The moment she entered my home..."

"My parents welcomed her warmly."

"They spoke to her for a long time."

"They liked her very much."

"And before leaving..."

"By the time she left, she no longer felt like a guest in our home."

For a brief moment, Siddu's smile reflected the warmth of those days.

Then it slowly disappeared.

"The semester holidays ended."

"I returned to college."

"And..."

He paused.

"That was when my love story slowly began to fall apart."

Sneha's smile faded.

"When I reached college, I called Shreya."

"She answered."

"But she sounded busy."

"She asked me to call her the next day."

"I didn't think much about it."

"So I waited."

"The next day..."

"I called again."

"No answer."

"The day after that..."

"The same."

His voice grew quieter.

"Then..."

"She started ignoring my calls again."

"This time..."

"It hurt even more than before."

"I tried calling her again and again."

"But nothing changed."

"I convinced myself that maybe her father had found out about us once again."

"So I tried to stay calm."

"I kept waiting for her call."

His eyes remained fixed on the distant mountains.

"But that call never came."

"The days turned into weeks."

"The weeks turned into months."

"And before I realized it..."

"Entire semesters had passed."

A heavy silence settled between them.

"Every single day..."

"I remembered her."

"I wondered if she was alright."

"I wondered if she was thinking about me."

"I never stopped believing she would come back."

He smiled faintly.

"Yashwanth never understood that."

"Whenever he saw me lost in thought, he would say..."

"'Stop thinking about her.'"

"'Girls these days are used to playing with boys' feelings.'"

"'Maybe Shreya is just like them.'"

Before Yashwanth could even finish his sentence...

"I always stopped him."

"'Don't say that,' I told him."

"'She isn't like everyone else.'"

"'She loves me.'"

"'She would never betray me.'"

"'I trust my Shreya more than anyone else.'"

Siddu fell silent.

A gentle breeze drifted across the mountains, carrying away his words.

Sneha looked at him quietly.

For the first time, she realized that even after everything he had endured, Siddu had never allowed hatred to replace the love he once had for Shreya.
